metadata.description: Actor dataset of core Soviet institutions (party, state, security, military, planning, youth) from 1917 to 1991.
metadata.introduction: A temporal registry of the governing institutions of the Soviet Union: the Communist Party and its leading organs, the supreme state bodies, the security and armed forces, the planning and banking system, and the youth league.

actors.name: Communist Party of the Soviet Union (CPSU)
actors.description: The founding and ruling political party of the Soviet Union, the institutional core of the one-party state; the only legal party and the source of policy for all state organs.

events.description: Founded as the Russian Social Democratic Labour Party at Minsk.
Bolsheviks seize power in the October Revolution.
Renamed the Russian Communist Party (Bolsheviks) at the 7th congress.
Renamed the Communist Party of the Soviet Union at the 19th congress.
Activities suspended by presidential decree; dissolved in the RSFSR.

actors.name: Politburo of the CPSU
actors.description: The highest policy-making authority of the Communist Party, directing the party, government, military and economy between congresses and plenums.

events.description: First Political Bureau elected by the Central Committee.
Reorganized into the Presidium at the 19th congress.
Restored as the Politburo at the 23rd congress.
Ceases to function as the party is suspended and Gorbachev resigns as General Secretary.

actors.name: Central Committee of the CPSU
actors.description: The party's leading collective between congresses, electing the Politburo, the Secretariat and the General Secretary and administering the party apparatus.

events.description: Elected at the RSDLP founding congress.
Creates the standing Politburo, Orgburo and Secretariat at the 8th congress.
Removes Nikita Khrushchev at a Central Committee plenum.
Dissolved with the suspension of the party.

actors.name: Supreme Soviet of the Soviet Union
actors.description: The highest legislative body of the Soviet state, sitting between sessions of the earlier congresses of soviets and electing the Presidium and the Council of Ministers.

events.description: Established by the 1936 (Stalin) Constitution.
First session of the first convocation convenes.
A reformed Supreme Soviet is elected by the new Congress of People's Deputies.
Dissolves itself, formalizing the end of the Soviet Union.

actors.name: Council of Ministers of the Soviet Union
actors.description: The highest executive and administrative body of the Soviet government, directing ministries, state committees and the economy under party control.

events.description: Formed as the Council of People's Commissars (Sovnarkom) of the USSR.
Reorganized as the Council of Ministers.
Abolished; replaced by the Interstate Economic Committee ahead of dissolution.

actors.name: KGB (Committee for State Security)
actors.description: The main security agency of the Soviet Union from 1954 to 1991, responsible for internal security, foreign intelligence, counter-intelligence and border troops; heir to the Cheka–NKVD lineage.

events.description: Founded as the Cheka under Felix Dzerzhinsky.
Becomes the NKVD, the Stalin-era security apparatus.
Established as the KGB, separated from the Interior Ministry.
Abolished and split into separate services by the State Council.

actors.name: Soviet Armed Forces (Red Army)
actors.description: The unified armed forces of the Soviet Union — army, navy, air force, air defence and strategic rocket forces — built from the Workers' and Peasants' Red Army of 1918.

events.description: Workers' and Peasants' Red Army founded during the Civil War.
Renamed the Soviet Army in the post-war reorganization.
Warsaw Pact signed, anchoring the Soviet-led alliance.
Dissolved; forces divided among the successor states.

actors.name: Gosplan (State Planning Committee)
actors.description: The central agency drafting the five-year plans and annual targets of the command economy, allocating resources across ministries and republics.

events.description: Founded as the State General Planning Commission.
First five-year plan begins, launching forced industrialization.
Sovnarkhoz reform devolves planning to regional economic councils under Khrushchev.
Abolished and replaced by the Ministry of Economics and Forecasting.

actors.name: Gosbank (State Bank)
actors.description: The central bank and sole issuing bank of the Soviet Union, financing the plan through state credit and supervising the monobank system.

events.description: Founded as the State Bank of the RSFSR under NEP.
Becomes the State Bank of the USSR.
Perestroika banking reform creates specialized state banks under Gosbank.
Dissolved; functions pass to the Central Bank of Russia.

actors.name: Komsomol (Young Communist League)
actors.description: The All-Union youth organization and the party's reserve: the mass channel for political socialization of Soviet youth aged 14 to 28.

events.description: Founded as the Russian Young Communist League.
Renamed the All-Union Leninist Communist Youth League.
Dissolves itself at its 22nd congress.
